blocks.text: Describes the three modes (plan, ask, accept-edits), the allow conditions (read/R0 everywhere, edit/R1 inside project in accept-edits, interact/R0 everywhere), and the catalog-is-a-copy rationale. States that this module is pure: no I/O, no logging, standard library only.
blocks.title: Module docstring

blocks.text: Defines the three decision strings, the three modes, the five risk levels, and the five tool classes (READ, EDIT, DELETE, SHELL, PLAN_EXIT, plus INTERACT from Patch L01a). ToolSpec is a frozen dataclass holding the tool's name, class, risk, optional risk_max, and argument type information. ceiling returns risk_max or risk.
blocks.title: Constants, tool classes, and ToolSpec

blocks.anchor: def _spec(name, cls, risk, required, types, risk_max=None) -> ToolSpec:
blocks.text: _spec builds a ToolSpec from positional arguments, computing the required/optional/types tuples from the types dict. TOOLS is the resulting Mapping, keyed by tool name, covering read_file, list_dir, glob, grep, edit_file, write_file, delete_path, bash, plan_exit, ask_user, and tasks.
blocks.title: Tool catalog construction

blocks.text: risk_rank maps R0–R4 to 0–4 and raises ValueError for anything else. max_risk returns whichever of two risk strings is higher. effective_risk delegates to max_risk and exists to give the protocol rule (client may raise, never lower) a named home.
blocks.title: Risk helpers

blocks.text: ModeDefault is a frozen dataclass with action and reason strings. _CLASS_CEILING records the highest risk a class may be allowed by default (READ: R0, EDIT: R1, INTERACT: R0; shell has none). mode_default handles PLAN_EXIT (always ask), INTERACT (allow at R0, else ask), READ (allow inside project at R0, else ask), and EDIT/DELETE/SHELL (deny in plan mode, deny on protected paths, allow edit in accept-edits at R1 inside project, else ask).
blocks.title: ModeDefault and mode_default

gotchas: The shell class has no ALLOW entry in mode_default at all — no mode ever allows running a process without approval
effective_risk only raises risk, never lowers it (the client's declared risk is taken if higher than the server's)
mode_default is NOT the same as the final decision: explicit allow/ask/deny rules in rules.py override it
An unknown tool class (e.g. an MCP tool) returns DENY from mode_default — the engine fails closed
how_it_works: TOOLS is built at import time by calling _spec for each tool; _spec constructs a ToolSpec with its required/optional/types tuples computed from the types dict
risk_rank converts an R0–R4 string to 0–4; max_risk and effective_risk use it to compare or raise the risk level
mode_default is a total function: it handles every combination of mode, tool_class, and risk and always returns a ModeDefault (never raises); unknown inputs return DENY
purpose: Provides two pure, importable artifacts: TOOLS (a Mapping from tool name to ToolSpec) and mode_default (a function that returns allow/ask/deny when no explicit rule matched). Both are used by the decide module. Having the catalog here rather than read from JSON means the policy engine never does I/O when deciding, and a test can verify catalog drift automatically.
summary: Defines the three permission modes, the hard-coded tool catalog, risk helpers, and the mode_default decision function for the m2c policy engine.

symbols.details: Total function: never raises, always returns a ModeDefault. Unknown mode or risk → deny. PLAN_EXIT → ask. INTERACT at R0 → allow, else ask. READ inside project at R0 → allow, else ask. EDIT/DELETE/SHELL in plan mode → deny; on protected path → deny; EDIT in accept-edits at R1 inside project → allow; otherwise ask. Unknown tool class → deny.
